verdicts.reason: A breaks the reading order: the headline sits at the very top above the product, the legal text is white and body-sized so it reads as a second message, and the sale banner and left-aligned CTA end up crammed at the bottom over a circle. B keeps the original sequence (logo, banner, bottle, headline, copy, CTA), but its logo is tiny and pushed top-right, the grey legal text is nearly as big as the body copy, and the oversized CTA competes with the headline.

A has the same flaws as the shared candidate: legal text close to body size, a heavy CTA and the logo off-centre top-right. B is more faithful in keeping the fine print small and the logo centred, but its bottle and headline are small, the CTA is undersized with tiny text, a large empty band sits between the copy and the CTA, and the legal text is too small to read at this width.

A puts the CTA at the top above the headline, which inverts the hierarchy. It shrinks the product to a tiny icon at the bottom, drops the visible logo, and leaves the sale banner floating low; its legal text is body-sized. B keeps a sensible order and readable sizes, though its legal text is too prominent and the logo is tiny and off-axis.

A jams the small bottle against the top edge, demotes the sale banner to below the copy, and moves the logo to the bottom, so brand-to-action order is lost; its legal text is also large. B keeps the original order with the logo up top, but still has over-sized legal text and a CTA that rivals the headline.
